title: Two Halves

source.quote: two or more individuals behave as though between them they form a single person.

setting: Planning meeting, Jules's third week on the team. Troy is walking through the architecture for next quarter's project.

L1.line: Don't worry about the architecture decision, Jules - I've already got it figured out. Just follow the plan I'll send you.
cues: Troy makes every call without asking Jules's view
Jules never offers an opinion, only ever nods and writes it down
both seem completely comfortable - no friction at all
L1.question: What's actually going on between Troy and Jules here?

options.text: A healthy division of labor - Troy's the manager, so naturally he decides.
options.feedback: Experience can be a real reason for one person deciding more - but notice Jules never even offers a view, not once. That's not experience speaking, that's an ego state shut down entirely.

options.text: A symbiosis - Troy is running Parent and Adult, Jules is running only Child, and between them they're using three ego states instead of six.
options.feedback: Right. Troy decides and directs (Parent plus Adult); Jules only ever assents (Child). Neither uses their full range - that's the Schiffs' definition of symbiosis, and the comfort both feel is part of the problem, not evidence it's fine.

options.text: A crossed transaction - Jules is refusing to engage with Troy directly.
options.feedback: No crossing here. Jules's silent nodding is actually complementary to Troy's Parent; the transaction flows smoothly, which is exactly what makes the symbiotic trap easy to miss.

L1.lesson: Symbiosis isn't about rank or who 'should' decide - it's that between two people, only three ego states are doing all the work: Troy supplies Parent and Adult, Jules supplies only Child, and the comfort both feel is what keeps it stable, not proof that it's healthy.

L2.intro: Troy's about to send you the architecture plan without ever asking what you think. You actually have a thought about it - what do you do?

beats.line: Don't worry about the architecture decision, Jules - I've already got it figured out. Just follow the plan I'll send you.

options.outcome: Troy nods, satisfied. The plan arrives an hour later. The symbiosis holds exactly as it was.
options.lesson: This is the easy, comfortable, default move - and that comfort is the tell. Taking the Child position confirms the symbiosis instead of disturbing it.

options.text: Are you sure? Maybe you should double check it with someone senior.
options.outcome: Troy waves it off. "No need, I've got this." Jules still hasn't said what Jules actually thinks.
options.lesson: This voices doubt, but it still hands the thinking to someone else rather than Jules's own Adult - it doesn't add the missing ego state back into the pair, it just relocates the Parent role to a third person.

options.text: Actually, I looked at this yesterday and I think there's a problem with the caching layer - can I walk you through it?
options.outcome: Troy pauses, surprised. "Oh - go ahead, I'm listening." For the first time in the scene, he's not deciding and Jules isn't just nodding.
options.lesson: Offering a real Adult observation - not a challenge, not a request for permission - is the move that adds a missing ego state back into the pair: now Jules is thinking, and Troy has to use his Adult to actually consider it instead of just directing.

options.text: You always just tell me what to do - I need you to ask my opinion sometimes.
options.outcome: Troy looks taken aback. "I... didn't realize I was doing that." Honest, but it's a complaint about the pattern rather than a concrete contribution to this decision.
options.lesson: True and worth saying eventually, but naming the pattern in the abstract doesn't itself add Adult content to this decision - pair it with an actual observation like the caching-layer one, or it just becomes a new topic to manage rather than a change in the symbiosis.

echo.setting: A month later: Jules notices a different teammate deferring to Troy on everything, the exact same old pattern.
echo.line: Don't worry about it, Troy's already got it figured out.
